close_reason: Core deviation mechanism complete: Deviation, DeviationStore, DeviationRunner; OSCAL investigation (jge.4) and expiry corpus (jge.3) remain open
description:
Operators need a first-class, auditable way to suppress or downgrade lint findings for legitimate local exceptions (CP waivers, interpretation memos, internal-CA deviations). Design requirements:

- Deviations are structured objects, not CLI flags or env vars
- Each deviation has: deviation_id, target_lint (specific lint ID), scope (issuer DN match, serial range, etc.), effective date range (expiry required), action (downgrade_severity_to, suppress), justification (text + optional evidence URI), authorized_by (signature or attribution)
- Deviations are signed by an operator-controlled key (not pkix-lint keys)
- Deviations are visible in output, not invisible: flagged as 'DEVIATION APPLIED by <id>' rather than suppressed silently
- Deviations are scoped — no wildcards on issuer, no 'suppress all for this lint ever'
- Deviations expire: after effective_end, the finding re-appears without renewal
- 'bd deviations list' equivalent: corpus of all active deviations is itself reportable/exportable
- No deviation packs ship inside the crate; vendor/CA packs must be loaded by the operator from operator-controlled storage
- Investigate OSCAL compatibility: NIST OSCAL Assessment Results profile has nearly identical semantics; federal customers already have OSCAL tooling

This is the mechanism behind 'you want it suppressed, write a local modification to the lint db.' Must be first-class and low-friction enough that operators with real waivers will use it, hostile enough to laundering that operators without real waivers cannot.

Reference: OSCAL, OPA/Rego policy bundles, CycloneDX VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) — steal schema ideas from VEX especially.
title: pkix-lint: design and implement deviation (waiver) mechanism
